title: Banana Processing & Waste-to-Wealth Models
subtitle: Two replicable cases for Andhra Pradesh districts: KVK Kanyakumari value-added foods and Jalgaon pseudo-stem processing cluster
source_note: Sources: TNAU Agritech Portal success story; RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

sections.title: Why banana processing matters for Andhra districts
sections.source: Sources: TNAU Agritech Portal success story; RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

items.desc: Converts perishable banana into marketable foods
Uses pseudo-stem, central core, sap and scutcher
Creates cottage-level processing and packaging work
Keeps value addition inside the mandal or cluster

blocks.label: OFFICER TAKEAWAY
blocks.text: Banana is not only a fruit crop. It is a full value chain: fruit, flower, pseudo-stem, fibre, sap, scutcher and central core can each be turned into income-generating products.

items: Fresh fruit glut can be managed through chips, flour, powder, candy, halwa and pickles.
Pseudo-stem disposal cost can be converted into farmer income and rural jobs.
District officers can converge horticulture, DRDA/SHG, PMFME, MSME and FPO support.

sections.title: Case Study 1: KVK Kanyakumari — value addition in banana
sections.source: Source: TNAU Agritech Portal, “success story - value addition in banana”

blocks.label: Training-led model
blocks.text: KVK Kanyakumari conducted a special programme on value addition in banana for farmers and farm women in banana-growing areas.

blocks.title: PRODUCT BASKET SHOWN TO FARMERS
items: Pseudostem pickle
Flower pickle
Unripe fruit pickle
Pseudostem candy
Fruit candy
Fruit halwa
Fruit powder
Flower vadagam
Nendran-based products

blocks.title: WHY IT IS PRACTICAL
items: Uses locally available fruit, flower and pseudo-stem inputs.
Can be started through SHG/FPO training without heavy capital expenditure.
Works well for farm women, rural youth and small food entrepreneurs.
Useful for AP districts where banana is grown but local processing is limited.

sections.title: How the Kanyakumari model works: from training to enterprise
sections.source: Source: TNAU Agritech Portal; application framework prepared for AP district officials

items.title: Mobilise
items.body: Identify banana growers, women SHGs and rural youth in banana mandals.

items.title: Train
items.body: Demonstrate recipes, hygiene, processing, shelf-life and packaging.

items.title: Standardise
items.body: Fix product standards: taste, weight, label, batch and expiry date.

items.title: Market
items.body: Sell through local fairs, retail outlets, institutions and online channels.

blocks.title: District/Mandal officer role
items: Select 2–3 banana villages per mandal for demonstration.
Link KVK / food technology institution / horticulture officer as technical partner.
Enable FSSAI registration, packaging design, brand name and basic bookkeeping.
Review sales, repeat orders and product quality every month.

sections.title: Case Study 2: Jalgaon — pseudo-stem waste-to-wealth cluster
sections.source: Source: RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

blocks.title: THE PROBLEM
items: Pseudo-stem after harvest was commonly thrown on field boundaries and burnt after drying.
Farmers faced disposal cost without income from a bulky biomass resource.
Jalgaon district alone generated around 38.5 lakh MT pseudo-stem biomass annually.

blocks.title: THE OPPORTUNITY
items: Extract fibre, sap and scutcher close to farms.
Use sap for organic liquid fertilizer and scutcher for compost/vermi-compost.
Create village-level cottage units operated by local farmer SHGs.

items.label: Functional cottage industrial units initially established
Paid to growers for pseudo-stem at unit

sections.source: Source: RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

blocks.label: Principle
blocks.text: localise bulky primary processing; centralise advanced processing and marketing.

blocks.title: Impact pathway
items: Farmer earns for pseudo-stem instead of paying disposal cost.
SHG-run cottage units generate local employment.
Sap and scutcher return to farming as low-cost inputs.
Central processing creates branding and market scale.

blocks.label: Message for AP
blocks.text: Review each banana cluster not only for area and production, but also for “processing potential” and “waste monetisation potential”.

sections.title: Lessons for Andhra Pradesh district and mandal officials
sections.source: Sources: TNAU Agritech Portal success story; RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

items.title: Start with clusters
items.body: Select banana-dense villages so raw material aggregation is viable.

items.title: Keep first processing local
items.body: Bulky pseudo-stem cannot travel long distances economically.

items.title: Use SHGs/FPOs
items.body: Women and farmer groups are ideal operators for food products and cottage units.

items.title: Standardise products
items.body: Recipes, packaging, label, FSSAI, batch tracking and quality control are essential.

items.title: Converge schemes
items.body: Horticulture + DRDA/SHG + PMFME + MSME + bank credit + KVK support.

items.title: Track outcomes
items.body: Measure income, jobs, waste processed, product sales and repeat buyers.

blocks.text: Do not begin with machinery purchase alone. Begin with cluster selection, entrepreneurs, technical recipes, market testing and confirmed raw material flow.

sections.title: How AP districts can adapt the models
sections.source: Sources: TNAU Agritech Portal success story; RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

cols.title: Fresh banana processing
items: Chips, flour, fruit powder, halwa, candy, pickle and ready-to-eat snacks.
Best for SHG/FPO-led units near production and consumption centres.
Use local fairs, schools/hostels, tourism points and retail shops for market testing.

cols.title: Pseudo-stem processing
items: Fibre extraction, sap collection, scutcher composting and central value addition.
Best for banana clusters with adequate post-harvest pseudo-stem availability.
Small units reduce transport cost; central unit handles branding and bulk sale.

cols.title: District-level enablers
items: District product plan and value-chain map.
Tie-up with KVK/TNAU/NRCB/food technology institutes.
Common brand, FSSAI handholding, packaging and buyer linkage.
Monthly review through agriculture/horticulture and livelihood KPIs.

blocks.label: Ideal first step
blocks.text: identify one banana cluster per district and run a 100-day pilot before scaling.

sections.title: Monitoring checklist: what to review every month
sections.source: Sources: TNAU Agritech Portal success story; RKVY/Tapti Valley Banana Pseudo-stem case document

groups.name: INPUT & PROCESS KPIs
items: No. of banana farmers/SHGs/FPOs mobilised
Quantity of fruit/pseudo-stem aggregated
No. of trainees completing practical training
Unit utilisation and days of operation

groups.name: OUTPUT KPIs
items: Kg/L of processed products produced
Kg/L sold and value realised
Packaging/branding/FSSAI registrations completed
Compost/liquid fertilizer supplied back to farmers

groups.name: OUTCOME KPIs
items: Additional income to farmers/SHGs
Jobs created for women/rural youth
Reduction in waste burning/disposal cost
Repeat buyers and market expansion

blocks.label: Closing message
blocks.text: For district and mandal officials, the banana case studies show how a crop-specific value chain can move from “production monitoring” to “income, enterprise and employment generation”.

blocks.label: Action after training
blocks.text: select one banana cluster, one food product pilot and one pseudo-stem waste-to-wealth pilot.
